new_findings.issue: Workflow hardening backlog. All 26 workflow files pin actions by tag (10 distinct, e.g. actions/checkout@v4), none by commit SHA. void.os android-ci.yml and resolver ci.yml declare no `permissions`, so they get the repository default token scope. 17 files use `ubuntu-latest`, which GitHub is moving to Ubuntu 26. There is no pull_request_target, no write-all, and no untrusted event text inside run steps.
evidence: inventory/workflow-audit.json (2026-11-04): 26 files parse; 26 with tag-pinned actions; 2 without permissions
new_findings.next_action: Apply SHA pinning, least-privilege permissions and pinned runner images together with the first hosted CI run after D-01, so the change is verified in the same run (plan rule: CI-only changes wait for CI)

new_findings.issue: The release keystore (termux-release.keystore and app/termux-release.keystore, PKCS12, certificate SHA-256 070cd54d…f68e) and keystore.properties with its store and key passwords were committed between 2025-07-30 (17f815b → 8c3857b) and remain in the public repository history. They were removed from HEAD on 2026-10-21 (f48d6c9), and the README already declares the key compromised. None of the four public release APKs is signed with it (F77).
evidence: `git log --all --diff-filter=A` lists both keystore files at 261234d (2025-07-30); keystore.properties in 17f815b, 4a23f32, adfbcfe, 261234d and 8c3857b carries non-placeholder 9-character passwords (values not recorded)
Certificate fingerprint read with keytool (password supplied from history through the environment, never printed): 070cd54d…f68e; the temporary keystore copies were deleted (2026-11-05)
new_findings.next_action: Treat the key as permanently revoked; never sign with it. Purging history needs an authorized history rewrite and would not undo the exposure (owner decision D-13)
